The organization manages several educational initiatives, including <cite id="3">Full Time and Part Time Hifz programs</cite>, a Nadira program, and a Sunday School. While the charity has seen significant financial growth, reporting <cite id="2">$2,799,757 in total revenue</cite> for FY2023, its spending patterns raise serious concerns regarding mission delivery. The organization maintains a <cite id="1">program expense ratio of 13.6%</cite>, which is significantly lower than the <cite id="1">75% industry standard</cite> and the <cite id="1">89.8% peer median</cite> for humanitarian and religious groups. Furthermore, a deeper analysis of its financial filings indicates a <cite id="1">program ratio score based on 14%</cite> spending, suggesting that a vast majority of donor funds are being held in reserve rather than being utilized for active community programming. The charity currently holds <cite id="1">63.0 months of working capital</cite> in working capital, an excessive amount that indicates a lack of urgency in deploying funds for their intended religious and educational purposes.
